prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.

worlds.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. In most years the crews' stakes show the surface within a few centimeters of where it stood the summer before. In three summers, 1962, 1988, and 2011, warm rain fell on the ice for weeks and the front broke into the valley in slabs the size of houses, and those three summers account for nearly all of the two kilometers the front has retreated. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
worlds.explanation: Almost all the loss came in three summers decades apart, with little change in between, so it was "sporadic." "Short-lived" fails because the front has retreated two kilometers and stayed back; "slight" fails because two kilometers is a quarter of the glacier; "stealthy" fails because house-sized slabs broke off in plain view.

short-lived.quote: two kilometers the front has retreated
short-lived.why: The front is still back, so the loss has not been undone.

slight.quote: nearly all of the two kilometers
slight.why: Two kilometers of an eight-kilometer glacier is a large loss.

stealthy.why: Loss by collapse in house-sized slabs was in plain sight.

worlds.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. Through the warm 1950s the front pulled back a little farther each summer, a full kilometer in all, leaving a strip of raw gravel. A run of snowy winters began in 1959, and the front pushed forward over that same gravel, flattening the young willows that had sprouted there; since 1966 its position has not shifted by more than a few meters. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
worlds.explanation: The glacier lost ice through the 1950s, then advanced back over the ground it had lost and has stayed there since 1966, so the loss was "short-lived." "Sporadic" fails because the front pulled back a little each summer; "slight" fails because it lost a full kilometer; "stealthy" fails because the retreat left raw gravel in plain view.

sporadic.why: Loss that came every year was not in scattered bursts.

slight.why: A kilometer of retreat is a large loss.

stealthy.quote: leaving a strip of raw gravel
stealthy.why: The retreat exposed open ground anyone could see.

worlds.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. The boulder the first crew painted at the edge of the front in 1950 now sits a short stroll from the ice, and radar shows the ice behind it nearly as thick as on the 1950 maps. Neighboring glaciers have lost a kilometer or more since then; this one, shaded by a high ridge and fed by heavy snow, has changed only by inches a year. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
worlds.explanation: The front has moved only a short stroll from a 1950 marker, the ice is nearly as thick as before, and the change came by inches a year, so the loss was "slight." "Sporadic" fails because it came steadily by inches a year; "short-lived" fails because the ice has not returned to the boulder; "stealthy" fails because radar shows the hidden ice is nearly as thick as ever.

sporadic.why: Loss spread evenly over every year was not in scattered bursts.

short-lived.quote: now sits a short stroll from the ice
short-lived.why: The ice has not come back to the 1950 marker, so the loss has not been undone.

stealthy.quote: nearly as thick as on the 1950 maps
stealthy.why: No large loss is hidden beneath the rock.

worlds.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. In every summer's photographs the rock-covered front rests against the same boulder it touched in 1950, and early surveyors listed this glacier as one of the few in the range holding steady. Radar soundings begun in 1995 found the ice under the rock sixty meters thinner than the 1950 maps show, and each year's sounding since has found it thinner by about the same amount. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
worlds.explanation: The photographs show no change, so surveyors thought the glacier was holding steady, while radar found sixty meters of thinning under the rock: the loss was "stealthy." "Sporadic" fails because it continues by about the same amount each year; "short-lived" fails because the thinning is still going on; "slight" fails because sixty meters is a large loss.

sporadic.why: A steady yearly loss was not in scattered bursts.

short-lived.quote: each year's sounding since has found it thinner
short-lived.why: Loss that continues to the present has not been undone.

slight.why: Sixty meters of thinning is a large loss.
